post.summary: Exchange an authorization code or a refresh token for a user access token
post.description: The token endpoint of the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow with PKCE. grant_type=authorization_code takes code, redirect_uri and code_verifier (and client_id for a public client); grant_type=refresh_token takes refresh_token and client_id. A confidential client authenticates with HTTP Basic over its Client ID and Client Secret.

200.description: The user access token, and a refresh token when the grant carries offline.access.

patches.why: X's OAuth 2.0 token endpoint: the document names it only as its OAuth2UserToken scheme's tokenUrl, and the Authorization Code Flow page documents it as a form-encoded POST taking code, grant_type, client_id, redirect_uri and code_verifier, or refresh_token, grant_type and client_id (https://docs.x.com/fundamentals/authentication/oauth-2-0/user-access-token)

source.quote: You can make a POST request to the following endpoint: https://api.x.com/2/oauth2/token

post.summary: Revoke a user access token or refresh token
post.description: Invalidates an access token or a refresh token, for an App to revoke a token it holds (a "log out"). A confidential client authenticates with HTTP Basic; a public client names its client_id.

patches.why: X's OAuth 2.0 revoke endpoint, which the document does not list: the Authorization Code Flow page documents it as a form-encoded POST of the token and the client_id (https://docs.x.com/fundamentals/authentication/oauth-2-0/user-access-token)

source.quote: if the App wants to programmatically revoke the access given to it: https://api.x.com/2/oauth2/revoke

post.summary: Obtain an OAuth request token (step 1 of the 3-legged OAuth flow and Sign in with X)
post.description: Allows a Consumer application to obtain an OAuth Request Token to request user authorization. oauth_callback is required (oob for out-of-band PIN mode); x_auth_access_type narrows the access level the application requests.

patches.why: X's OAuth 1.0a request_token leg, outside the v2 document: the OAuth API reference documents its resource URL and its oauth_callback and x_auth_access_type parameters (https://docs.x.com/fundamentals/authentication/api-reference)

post.summary: Exchange an authorized request token for an access token (step 3 of the 3-legged OAuth flow)
post.description: Allows a Consumer application to exchange the OAuth Request Token for an OAuth Access Token. oauth_token is the request token, and oauth_verifier the verifier the callback carried (or the PIN, out of band).

200.description: oauth_token, oauth_token_secret, user_id and screen_name, form-encoded.

patches.why: X's OAuth 1.0a access_token leg, outside the v2 document: the OAuth API reference documents its resource URL and its oauth_token and oauth_verifier parameters (https://docs.x.com/fundamentals/authentication/api-reference)

post.summary: Revoke an issued OAuth access token
post.description: Allows a registered application to revoke an issued OAuth access_token, signed in user context with the access token to invalidate.

patches.why: X's OAuth 1.0a invalidate_token, outside the v2 document: the OAuth API reference gives its resource URL (https://docs.x.com/fundamentals/authentication/api-reference)

post.summary: Revoke an issued OAuth access token (the .json form of the resource URL)
post.description: The same invalidate_token, at the URL the API reference's own example request posts to.

patches.why: X's OAuth 1.0a invalidate_token as the OAuth API reference's example request sends it, with the v1.1 .json suffix (https://docs.x.com/fundamentals/authentication/api-reference)

impression_count.description: Number of times this Post has been viewed.

like_count.description: Number of likes on this Post.

quote_count.description: Number of quote Posts of this Post.

reply_count.description: Number of replies to this Post.

retweet_count.description: Number of times this Post has been reposted.
